subject: Pilot extension & alternative billing models for NimbleHealth trial
messages:
From: Claire Evans <claire@nimblehealth.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot extension request + alternative billing model

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from our side — we hit a few integration delays on the NimbleHealth side and won't get the usage spike we expected in the originally scheduled 30-day pilot. The team would like to request a 6-week extension to validate performance at volume.

Two things we'd like to explore rather than a straight time-only extension:
- A performance-linked slab where we pay by successful inference events (with a predictable monthly cap) while we ramp.
- Or adding a temporary committed "seat" (throughput unit) for the extension so we get predictable latency during tests and Redwood can keep revenue predictable.

Can you share pricing sketches for both approaches and any constraints (min commit, overage caps, conversion credits if we convert to a paid contract)? Our procurement lead Tom Hsu (cc'd) will handle PO details.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Evans
Head of Product
NimbleHealth
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Evans <claire@nimblehealth.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request + alternative billing model

Claire — thanks for the heads up and totally reasonable ask. We can support either approach; below are two pragmatic, short-duration options we use frequently. I've attached a one-page summary (nimble-pilot-amendment-v1.pdf).

Option A — Performance slab (recommended if you want usage-aligned pricing)
- 4 tier slabs by successful inference events/month (0-5M / 5-20M / 20-75M / 75M+)
- Blended unit rate with automatic tiering and a hard overage cap (we cap monthly spend to X% over projected tier)
- No minimum commit required for extension; 6-week term priced pro rata.
- If you convert to a committed contract within 90 days, we apply a credit equal to 30% of extension spend toward the first 12 months.

Option B — Temporary seat / throughput commit (recommended if predictability is critical)
- Reserve dedicated throughput seats (e.g., 2 seats = ~200 RPS sustained) for 6 weeks at a flat weekly rate.
- Includes a 10% conversion credit off the first-year committed price if you sign within 60 days.
- We can waive the one-time onboarding fee for the extension.

To size this accurately I need your expected peak RPS for the test window and an approximate monthly successful-inference target. If you prefer, we can price both and I’ll send an amendment and DocuSign link.

Attachments: nimble-pilot-amendment-v1.pdf (summary), usage-estimate-nimble.csv (blank template)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pilot extension request + alternative billing model — recommendation

Marissa / Ben — forwarding NimbleHealth's ask. My read: they prefer predictability but want to avoid a large upfront commit. I recommend we pitch Option B with a 6-week seat reservation and the following concessions to close quickly:
- 15% off the seat list rate for the 6-week extension (one-time concession)
- Waive onboarding fee for the extension
- Add a conversion milestone: if they sign a 12-month committed agreement within 60 days after the extension, Redwood will credit 25% of the extension fees toward the first invoice (finance-friendly, not full rebate).

Rationale: seats make their engineering tests deterministic and reduce the chance of them hitting noisy results that derail the evaluation. The conversion credit preserves upside if they convert.

Key asks from finance/legal: confirm we can structure the credit as an invoice-level credit (not a refund) and that legal is comfortable with a 60-day conversion window. Also confirm we can cap overage at +20% of the weekly seat charge (so we don't have unbounded risk).

Thanks — want to move quickly here.

Jonas

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Claire — thanks for the heads up and totally reasonable ask...
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot extension request + alternative billing model — recommendation

Jonas — agree with Option B as primary. Approve the 15% concession and waived onboarding fee.
Two small tweaks:
- Make the conversion credit 25% of extension fees (you proposed 25% — confirm that's our offer), and require the contract to be at least a 12-month commit to trigger it.
- Keep the overage cap language explicit in the amendment (max +20% weekly charge).

If Ben signs off on the credit structure from finance, you have my go-ahead to send the amendment and DocuSign link.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Evans <claire@nimblehealth.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@nimblehealth.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot amendment (6-week seat reservation) — NimbleHealth

Claire — thanks — based on our internal alignment I've attached the formal amendment (nimble-pilot-amendment-v1.pdf) and a blank usage template. Summary of the agreed options:

Chosen path: Option B — 6-week reserved seats (temporary throughput units)
- Reservation: 2 seats (~200 RPS sustained) for 6 weeks
- Extension fee: list = $18,000 (6 weeks) — applied concession: 15% off => $15,300 total
- Onboarding fee waived for the extension
- Conversion credit: 25% of extension fees ($3,825) applied as invoice credit if NimbleHealth signs a 12-month committed agreement within 60 days of extension end
- Overage cap: any usage beyond the reserved throughput billed at 1.2x weekly seat charge, capped at +20% of the weekly charge in a given week

Next steps:
1) Review amendment PDF.
2) If acceptable, sign via DocuSign (link below) and Ben/Finance will issue an invoice.
3) If you prefer the performance slab instead, tell me and I’ll send Option A pricing instead.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/CL-555-abc
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/HL-98765

Attachments: nimble-pilot-amendment-v1.pdf, usage-estimate-nimble.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
